clue.text: There's no lack of trying here

definitions.text: There's no lack of trying here

parts.words: There's no lack of trying here
parts.note: trying reads as making an effort, but it is the legal sense: hearing cases, so there is plenty of it in this place

explanation.surface: A place where everyone puts in plenty of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' suggests effort; the clue means trying cases before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Cases are tried by judges in a building of the legal system, so trials are constantly happening there.

clue.text: Man with pipe loses head — could be in the attic?

indicators.note: loses head means the first letter of the word for the tradesman is dropped

parts.note: a plumber is a tradesman who works with pipes

explanation.surface: A plumber gets decapitated, and the body ends up stored upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' drops the P from PLUMBER. Lumber, in British use, is disused furniture and junk stored away.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumber is old junk and disused furniture, the sort of clutter stored in a loft.

clue.text: Fool following success in ad-lib

indicators.note: following means the word for fool comes after the word for success

parts.note: to win is to have success
git is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot coming after a triumph improvises.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise without preparation is to do something without a script.

clue.text: What sportsman likes to be on the bench?

parts.note: a form is a long bench without a back, as in an old schoolroom

explanation.surface: A player would hate to be sitting on the substitutes' bench.
explanation.walkthrough: The bench suggests a substitute, but a FORM is a backless bench.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman wants to be playing well, at the top of his game.

clue.text: Uncompromising army unit didn't give away so much

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
if you lent less you parted with fewer things on loan

explanation.surface: A hard-line military outfit was stingy with its generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Relentless means unyielding and harsh, refusing to soften.

clue.text: Cuts in, and gets goals

definitions.meaning: to score a surface is to cut lines into it
a team ... when it gets goals

explanation.surface: A striker darts inside and finds the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring is both scratching a mark into something and adding points in a game.

clue.text: The cold's gone but you need to relax

definitions.meaning: a chill is out, as if a cold had been driven away
to unwind or take it easy

explanation.surface: Once your cold has cleared up you should take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial phrase meaning unwind, which literally reads as the coldness being expelled.

clue.text: Kinsman's account

definitions.meaning: a narration or telling of events

explanation.surface: A relative gives his version of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative is a family member; the word also means a narrative or report of something told.

clue.text: County built round a very soft stone

indicators.note: built round means the county word is put up around the other letters

parts.note: a shire is an English county
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A county is constructed around a very soft rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious gemstone, usually blue.

clue.text: Part of engine having many uses

definitions.meaning: the pipe assembly that distributes air or exhaust between cylinders
multiple and varied, an old sense of the word

explanation.surface: An engine component is versatile.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a branching pipe in engines and also means numerous or of many kinds.

clue.text: Sounds like the man for a boost

indicators.note: sounds like means the man's name is spoken to give a word with a different spelling

parts.note: Philip is a man's name

explanation.surface: The name of a chap is said to give encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or something that gives a lift to spirits.

clue.text: School term gain for one in a new place

indicators.note: to school is to train or drill, so these letters are disciplined into a new order

explanation.surface: A school term brings an advantage to a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun but is a verb, training the letters of TERM GAIN into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant has left their homeland to settle in another country.

clue.text: Good central heating about switched on. There's a temporary difficulty

indicators.note: about means the good and heating letters go around the next piece

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for central heating, as in estate agents' listings
a light switched on is lit

explanation.surface: A good heating system has been turned on, but there is a hitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a minor malfunction or snag that interrupts things briefly.

clue.text: Substitute finds tar on building

indicators.note: building means these letters are constructed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A replacement worker discovers tar on a construction site.
explanation.walkthrough: As held, 'car' gives a C where the answer needs a T; the anagram works only with 'tar'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to act in place of someone, which is what a substitute does.

clue.text: This dish is recommended not only in Paris

definitions.text: This dish is recommended not only in Paris

parts.words: This dish is recommended not only in Paris
parts.note: a French phrase for the day's special on a menu, used in restaurants well beyond France

explanation.surface: A recommended dish turns up outside Paris too.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for the special of the day is borrowed by English menus too.

clue.text: Sailors in vessels raising certain type of bottle

indicators.note: in means the sailors are placed inside the vessels
raising means the word for vessels reads upwards in this down entry

parts.note: pots are vessels
a crew is a ship's company of sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors in ships are hoisting a particular bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'raising' turns the vessels word upwards, giving STOP; 'in' then places the sailors inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle sealed with a threaded cap rather than a cork.

clue.text: Nuts supply fit for crackers

indicators.note: supply as an adverb means flexibly, so these letters bend into another order

parts.note: fit means able, as in fit for duty

explanation.surface: Nuts supply something suitable to go with crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' and 'crackers' look like food; 'supply' is the adverb of supple, bending NUTS into UNST.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is slang for mad, and an unbalanced mind is mentally erratic.

clue.text: Aware of most of tennis set played

indicators.note: played means the letters are rearranged, as if put into play
most of means the last letter of tennis is dropped

explanation.surface: Conscious of most of a tennis set being played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims tennis to TENNI; 'played' rearranges TENNI with SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being is conscious and capable of perception.

clue.text: Study slope of a region that's familiar

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a versant is the slope or side of a mountain range

explanation.surface: Examine the slope of a region you already know.
explanation.definitionFit: Being conversant with something means being well acquainted with it.

clue.text: Church assistant to be in charge of museum

definitions.meaning: an assistant to a parish priest in the Church of England
to organise and look after a collection or exhibition

explanation.surface: A clergyman's helper is going to run a museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a junior Anglican clergyman and, as a verb, means to manage an exhibition.

clue.text: He's some contraband items possibly

indicators.note: some means only part of the words contraband items is used, letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A man who may well carry smuggled goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw or robber might well be dealing in smuggled goods.

clue.text: Army type, we hear, seen at the centre

indicators.note: we hear means the officer's rank is spoken, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: a colonel is an army officer

explanation.surface: A soldier is said to be found in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the core or heart of something.

clue.text: Property development required immediately in outskirts of Eastboume

indicators.note: in means the word for immediately sits inside the edges of the town name
outskirts of means the first and last letters of the town name

parts.note: stat is medical jargon for immediately

explanation.surface: A housing project needed right away on the edge of Eastbourne, a south-coast English town.
explanation.definitionFit: A housing estate is a planned development of homes.

clue.text: Put on suit having meal out

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Wear a suit when eating out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' reads as dressing, but means to feign.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a show of something is to fake or pretend it.

clue.text: What may be in prescription could display inscription!

definitions.meaning: a pill a doctor might prescribe
a flat slab with lettering carved into it

explanation.surface: A medicine on prescription bears writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a pill and a stone slab carrying engraved words.

clue.text: Cricket sides appear occasionally

definitions.meaning: in cricket the off side and the on (leg) side are the two halves of the field

explanation.surface: Some cricket teams turn up now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the off side and the on side, which together give the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something intermittently means doing it now and again.

clue.text: Folds, using staple

indicators.note: using means the letters of staple are put to a new use in another order

explanation.surface: Folding something by means of a staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleats are folds pressed or sewn into fabric.

clue.text: Unusual ant found in college in the east

indicators.note: found in means the jumbled ant goes inside the college

parts.note: Oriel is a college of Oxford University

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of ant are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange ant is discovered in a college out east.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means eastern, from or situated in the Orient.
